changes_since_r43: Adaptive Buyer Experience: category_strategy_answer and commercial_signal_answer are now rendered by the frontend (previously computed but never displayed) -- dedicated renderers matching each experience's natural information needs (category position/supplier strategy/opportunities/roadmap for strategy; what changed/what it may mean/where I would look for signals).
Signal headline fix: the 'signal' summary sentence is now derived from the actual calculated spend/volume growth figures when available, replacing a hard-coded generic sentence.

Adaptive Depth: section visibility within each of the four experiences now reflects materiality, not mere data presence -- MONEY only shown when a reliable calculation exists, a genuine 'WHAT IS MISSING' section added for supplier requests, category-strategy roadmap horizons containing only boilerplate 'not yet supported by evidence' status are dropped from the primary answer, problem-solving OPTIONS is suppressed once the root cause is established and the decision is made (kept fully in the underlying data for audit/deep-dive).

Dynamic Experience principle codified as a permanent, standing comment at the answer-composition dispatch point in app/static/index.html, with five new regression tests proving both halves: materially different situations produce materially different section-driving data, and materially identical situations produce identical results across independent requests (never randomly varying).

Cross-contamination guard (app/pipeline/reasoner.py): the three case_mode-specific prompt injections (supplier_request/commercial_signal/category_strategy) no longer fire for a problem_solving case, closing a bug where an inferred or accidentally-selected case_mode could inject a misleading 'you are reasoning through a supplier request' frame onto an unrelated problem-solving case.
Fourth front-door tile ('A problem I need to solve') added to both the hero grid and the activity panel, routing via free-text classification with no case_mode forced.

Problem-solving buyer-facing answer restructured to WHAT'S HAPPENING / WHAT WE KNOW / WHAT WE DON'T KNOW YET / OPTIONS / MY RECOMMENDATION / NEXT STEP / WHAT COULD CHANGE THIS, with deterministic (never model-generated) safety templates for the OEM-conflict-of-interest and unproven-economics cases.
capabilities_included: Commercial Intelligence Kernel -- single evidence/truth layer shared by every reasoning profile
Supplier Request, Commercial Signal, Category Strategy reasoning profiles, all now rendered as distinct buyer experiences
Dependency-aware category roadmap with real prerequisite chains and decision gates
Unknown -> Investigation conversion for material market/ESG evidence gaps

Complex Problem Solving vertical slice: Problem -> Evidence -> Root Cause -> Countermeasure -> Action -> Outcome, Maersk principle enforced structurally, validated against supplier/commercial, procurement/process, and asset/obsolescence proof cases
Provider-independent LLM client abstraction across all five model-calling files
Safe buyer-facing transport -- diagnostics excluded from the default API response

Adaptive answer composition -- each of the four front-door experiences renders its own natural section set, adapted further within each case by evidence materiality and decision stage, not fixed to a rigid template
Four-tile front door with preserved free-text classification
known_limitations: market_verification.py's use of Anthropic's server-side web_search tool remains a genuine, undisguised exception to provider independence.

Supplier Request's negotiation-section gating depends on the model's own judgment of when negotiation is genuinely warranted; that gating exists structurally but has not been independently verified against a live model in this environment.
Category Strategy's SUPPLIER STRATEGY section suppression is all-or-nothing (empty vs populated), not yet graded by evidence strength within a populated section.
No live external market or ESG data source anywhere in this build.
Complex Problem Solving does not cover Gemba, advanced charting, recurrence learning, or proactive monitoring -- explicitly out of scope by design.
supplier_request_answer and commercial_signal_answer do not carry the same explicit 'diagnostics' separation as category_strategy_answer and problem_solving_answer.
The cross-dimension trade-off detector (category strategy roadmap) uses generic capitalized-word matching -- known, previously-recorded precision limitation, unchanged.
No live Claude/Anthropic API access exists anywhere in this build or the environment that produced it. Every test, including all HTTP-path tests, is deterministic and mock-based.

configuration_requirements.database: PostgreSQL 16, schema at db/schema.sql -- additive/idempotent migrations only, safe against any prior database in this lineage.

migration_requirements: Run db/schema.sql. No new migrations in this release beyond what R42 already introduced (the classified_content_type CHECK constraint widening).
packaging_notes: No secrets, real API keys, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, or local caches included. .env.example/.env.test.example contain only placeholder values, confirmed by direct inspection before packaging. Working tree unchanged between the final regression run (643 passed) and this ZIP's creation -- no application code was modified after that run.
